Russian women outlive Russian men by about 10.6 years. In the Netherlands the gap is under 3. The further east you go in Europe, the wider it gets.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ This map shows female minus male life expectancy at birth in 2024. Women live longer in every country on it, but the size of the gap varies almost fourfold across the continent.
2/ The smallest gaps sit in the northwest: the Netherlands 2.8 years, Sweden 3.0, Norway 3.2, Iceland and Ireland 3.3, the UK and Denmark 3.8.
3/ Then it climbs as you move east and south: Germany 4.7, France 5.7, Czechia 5.9, Hungary 6.2, Poland 7.4, Romania 7.5.
4/ And the darkest band: Estonia and Lithuania 8.6, Moldova 9.0, Belarus 9.5, Ukraine 9.6, Latvia 9.9 and Russia 10.6.

5/ Why do women live longer at all? Historically men have used more tobacco, alcohol and drugs and died more often of the diseases linked to them, as well as of injuries, from car crashes to suicide. Biology plays a part too.
6/ Those same risk factors help explain the map. Heavy smoking and drinking among men are commonly cited for the wide gaps in the former Soviet states, which fill the dark end of the scale.
Data: World Bank (UN WPP 2024). Does the gap in your country surprise you? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
